Subject: Quick: mid-contract capacity add + co-term question

Hi Priyom,

We’re planning a mid-quarter bump for our ML inference usage and expect to add roughly 200M tokens/month starting Jan. We’d like to: 1) get a clear price for the incremental units, 2) see options to co-term to our fiscal year end (Mar 31), and 3) understand any short-term credits you’d be willing to provide during the transition window. Procurement wants an outline by EOD Fri so they can start the amendment review.

Subject: RE: Quick: mid-contract capacity add + co-term question

Hi Lina — thanks for the heads up and the forecast. Short answer: we can do a clean path that minimizes operational churn. I’ll outline two pragmatic options below and attach a short proposal PDF.

Option A — Staged uplift + bridge credit (recommended)
- Immediate add: +200M tokens/mo on current plan, billed at standard overage rate for month 1.
- Bridge credit: apply a one-time 10% invoice credit on the incremental usage months (Jan–Mar) to offset ramp uncertainty.
- Co-term: annualize the incremental capacity (convert to a committed top-up) at co-term to 2027-03-31 with a 10% discounted rate on the additional committed units if signed by Jan 15.

Option B — Burst capacity + voucher
- Short-term reserved burst pool for Jan–Mar with a fixed monthly voucher; no change to current contract term.
- Lower administrative overhead but slightly higher per-unit cost.

Internal note: If Acme signs to annualize early we can extend deeper discount (12%) — needs finance approval.

Next steps: I’ve attached AcmeAI_Midterm_PROPOSAL_v1.pdf with example numbers and a draft amendment. Lauren — can you flag any legal / procurement language concerns? Ben — can finance stretch to 12% on the incremental committed units if they annualize now?

Doc attachments: AcmeAI_Midterm_PROPOSAL_v1.pdf (proposal), co-term-checklist.xlsx (procurement checklist)

Thanks — I’ll hold a short call if that’s helpful.

Priyom — quick thoughts from pricing:
- Standard practice is 10% on new committed top-ups if signed mid-term. Finance can approve up to 12% in special situations (strategic account, multi-year intent), but we should capture clear commitment language and an exec sponsor on the Acme side.
- If they choose the burst/voucher path, margin is ~6–8% higher; we can still offer a token credit, but not the annualize discount band.

If you want to push to 12% we need: 1) a signed amendment with co-term date, 2) a short commercial approval form (I’ll get that), and 3) a note in HubSpot for discount justification. I added a HubSpot link in the related links.

Priyom / Ben — legal and procurement notes:
- Procurement will ask to preserve existing SLA language; do not change uptime/SLA commitments in the amendment.
- We should avoid multi-year pricing guarantees beyond the co-term date; propose the committed top-up with a defined termination/true-up clause at the new co-term.
- Suggest offering 9% as the standard co-term incentive, with a one-time 3-month bridge credit (10% equivalent) to smooth the billing transition. That keeps us from needing exec-level pricing approval but is attractive to the customer.

I’ve attached a co-term checklist (co-term-checklist.xlsx) with the procurement and legal signoffs we typically require. If they push for 12% have them get a revenue exec on the thread.
